{{nihongo|'''Izumoiwai Shrine, Moroyama'''|出雲伊波比神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Moroyama, Saitama|ar|موروياما|arz|موروياما|ceb|Moroyama-machi|de|Moroyama (Saitama)|es|Moroyama|fa|مورویاما، سایتاما|fr|Moroyama|id|Moroyama, Saitama|it|Moroyama|ja|毛呂山町|ko|모로야마정|ms|Moroyama, Saitama|my|မိုရိုယာမမြို့၊ ဆိုင်းတမ|pl|Moroyama|ru|Морояма|sv|Moroyama|tl|Moroyama, Saitama|tr|Moroyama|uk|Морояма (Сайтама)|ur|مورویاما، سائیتاما|zh|毛呂山町|qid=Q1354799}}, {{ill|Iruma District, Saitama|ceb|Iruma-gun|fr|District d'Iruma|id|Distrik Iruma, Saitama|it|Distretto di Iruma|ja|入間郡|ko|이루마군|pl|Powiat Iruma|ru|Ирума (уезд)|uk|Повіт Ірума|zh|入間郡|qid=Q1153801}}, {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|Q128186|qid=Q128186}}. Its former shrine rank was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. It is considered one of the candidate shrines (ronsha) for the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shikinaisha (minor shrine)}} listed as “{{ill|Izumo Iwai Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|出雲伊波比神社 (曖昧さ回避)|qid=Q104539298|lt=Izumo Iwai Shrine}}.” {{nihongo|'''Izumoiwai Shrine, Moroyama'''|出雲伊波比神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Musashi Province]].

It is the only shrine in Saitama Prefecture where {{ill|Yabusame|Q1886157|qid=Q1886157}} (mounted archery) is offered annually.

== History ==
According to shrine tradition (the “Garyūzan Gūdenki”), in the 53rd year of {{ill|Emperor Keikō|Q329723|qid=Q329723}}, {{ill|Yamato Takeru|lt=Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258}} enshrined {{ill|Ōkuninushi|abstract|Q276944|ca|Ōkuninushi|es|Ōkuninushi|fa|اوکونینوشی|fr|Ōkuninushi|hu|Ókuninusi|id|Ookuninushi|it|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主|ko|오오쿠니누시|mni|ꯑꯣꯀꯨꯅꯤꯅꯨꯁꯤ|pl|Ōkuninushi|pt|Ookuninushi|ru|Окунинуси|simple|Ōkuninushi|sr|Okuninuši|sv|Ōkuninushi|tr|Ōkuninushi|uk|Окунінуші|vi|Ōkuninushi|zh|大國主|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto}} after dedicating a halberd bestowed by the emperor. Later, during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seimu|Q316672|qid=Q316672}}, the Musashi {{ill|Kuni no miyatsuko|Q2483673|qid=Q2483673}} enshrined {{ill|Ame no Hohi|Q10940685|qid=Q10940685}}, forming the deity Izumo Iwai no Kami.<ref name="moro">[http://www.town.moroyama.saitama.jp/www/contents/1285113266909/index.html Izumo Iwai Shrine] – Moroyama Town website</ref>

Records in a Daijō-kan edict indicate that in the 3rd year of {{ill|Hōki|Q18520676|qid=Q18520676}} ({{ill|772|ab|772|af|772|am|772 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|772|ar|772|ary|772|ast|772|az|772|azb|۷۷۲ (میلادی)|bar|772|bcl|772|be|772|be_x_old|772|bg|772|bn|৭৭২|bpy|মারি ৭৭২|br|772|bs|772.|ca|772|cdo|772 nièng|ceb|772|ckb|٧٧٢|crh|772|cs|772|cv|772|cy|772|da|772|de|772|el|772|eml|772|eo|772|es|772|et|772|eu|772|fa|۷۷۲ (میلادی)|fi|772|fo|772|fr|772|fy|772|ga|772|gan|772年|gd|772|gl|772|he|772|hi|772|hr|772.|ht|772 (almanak jilyen)|hu|772|hy|772|id|772|io|772|is|772|it|772|ja|772年|jv|772|ka|772|kk|772 жыл|ko|772년|la|772|lb|772|lij|772|lmo|772|lt|772 m.|map_bms|772|mdf|772|mg|772|mhr|772|mk|772|mr|इ.स. ७७२|mrj|772 и|ms|772|mzn|۷۷۲|nah|772|nap|772|nds|772|nds_nl|772|new|सन् ७७२|nl|772|nn|772|no|772|nrm|772|nso|772|oc|772|or|୭୭୨|os|772-æм аз|pl|772|pnb|772|pt|772|qu|772|ro|772|ru|772 год|rue|772|sa|७७२|scn|772|sd|772ع|sh|772.|shn|772|si|772|sk|772|sl|772|smn|772|sq|772|sr|772|su|772|sv|772|sw|772|tg|Соли 772|th|พ.ศ. 1315|tk|772|tl|772|tly|772|tr|772|tt|772 ел|uk|772|ur|772ء|uz|772|vec|772|vi|772|war|772|wuu|772年|xmf|772|zh|772年|zh_min_nan|772 nî|zh_yue|772年|qid=Q30729}}) of the {{ill|Nara period|Q189178|qid=Q189178}}, the shrine received offerings ({{ill|Hanpei|Q11481885|qid=Q11481885}}) as an official shrine.<ref name="moro"/>

In the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} listed it as the foremost of the five shrines in Iruma District.<ref name="moro"/>

The present shrine buildings were rebuilt in the year following a fire in the 7th year of {{ill|Daiei (era)|Q1193564|qid=Q1193564}} ({{ill|1527|Q6412|qid=Q6412}}).<ref name="moro"/>

== Cultural Properties ==
== Important Cultural Property (National Designation) ==
* Main hall (with two ridge plaques): Ikken-sha nagare-zukuri, copper-sheet roofing, built in the 8th year of Daiei (1528).<ref>[https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/184606 Cultural Heritage Online]</ref>

== Yabusame ==
The shrine’s yabusame is said to have originated in the 6th year of {{ill|Kōhei|Q1193572|qid=Q1193572}} ({{ill|1063|Q19400|qid=Q19400}}), when it was dedicated by {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|Q32613|qid=Q32613}}.<ref name="morop">{{PDFlink|[http://www.town.moroyama.saitama.jp/www/contents/1588308692078/files/1.pdf Yabusame of Izumo Iwai Shrine]}} – Moroyama Town pamphlet</ref> As of the 2010s, it is held twice a year, in spring and autumn. In spring, a ritual called ganteki is performed in which boys under the age of seven ride a horse and shoot a single arrow.<ref name="morop"/> Full-scale mounted archery (yūteki) is carried out during the main autumn festival, where boys around 15 years old ride and perform three rounds of shooting using three horses (one from each festival district).<ref name="morop"/>

Date and time (main festival): Every year on {{ill|November 3|Q2995|qid=Q2995}} ({{ill|Culture Day|Q1009535|qid=Q1009535}})
: Morning shooting: from around 9:00 a.m. to about 10:30 a.m.
: Evening shooting: from 2:30 p.m. to about 5:00 p.m.

== Other ==
In 2016, it was reported that a large number of {{ill|Feral cat|Q2404562|qid=Q2404562}} had settled on the shrine grounds, causing problems.<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese|url=http://www.saitama-np.co.jp/news/2016/11/13/07.html |title=Cries at the Cat Shrine… Important Cultural Property Shrine in Moroyama, Increased Cats Scratching with Claws; Feeding Stopped (Saitama Shimbun, November 12, 2016) |accessdate=May 21, 2017 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20161113195807/http://www.saitama-np.co.jp/news/2016/11/13/07.html |archivedate=November 13, 2016 }}</ref>

== Access ==
* 5-minute walk from {{ill|Moro Station|Q844988|qid=Q844988}} on the {{ill|Hachikō Line|Q1372071|qid=Q1372071}} of {{ill|East Japan Railway Company|Q499071|qid=Q499071|lt=JR East}}
* 10-minute walk from {{ill|Higashi-Moro Station|Q11527554|qid=Q11527554}} on the {{ill|Tobu Ogose Line|Q2782450|qid=Q2782450}}
* About 15 minutes by car from {{ill|Tsurugashima interchange|Q11174029|qid=Q11174029}} on the {{ill|Kan-etsu Expressway|Q1059893|qid=Q1059893}} or {{ill|Ken-o-Tsurugashima interchange|Q11422768|qid=Q11422768}} on the {{ill|Ken-Ō Expressway|Q5957728|qid=Q5957728}}
